rich_summary: In the public assembly, the sage Valmiki solemnly testifies to Sita’s absolute purity, swearing the truth of his words on the power of his long ascetic life. Rama acknowledges that he already believed in Sita’s innocence but had banished her out of fear of public opinion. He accepts Lava and Kusha as his sons and seeks reconciliation before the gathered court. Drawn by the gravity of the moment, hosts of gods, sages, and celestial beings assemble to witness Sita’s final vindication. Sita then makes a final oath that she has never thought of any man but Rama. In response, the Earth itself opens: the goddess Dharani rises with a jeweled throne borne by mighty Nagas and receives Sita into her arms. As Sita descends into the Earth, the cosmos trembles and the gods acclaim her supreme virtue.

highlight_spans.why: Valmiki invokes the power of his ascetic truth to declare Sita’s innocence, establishing divine authority behind her vindication.
Rama admits he banished Sita not from doubt but from fear of public condemnation, revealing the tragic conflict between kingship and personal truth.
Sita’s final oath of fidelity to Rama becomes the emotional climax that triggers the miraculous response of the Earth.
The pivotal miracle: the Earth goddess rises with a celestial throne borne by Nagas and receives Sita, confirming her purity through divine intervention.
The cosmic reaction—gods, beings, and the trembling world—underscores the mythic scale of Sita’s departure and her transformation into a sacred figure.

top_scenes.scene_text: Sita stands before the vast assembly of kings, sages, and gods with folded hands, yellow robes flowing, as she swears her final oath of fidelity to Rama.
The Earth splits open and a radiant throne supported by jeweled Nagas rises upward while the Earth goddess Dharani embraces Sita amid falling celestial flowers.
As Sita descends into the Earth in Dharani’s arms, gods in the sky shower blossoms while the assembled world—kings, sages, and creatures—watch in stunned awe.
